answer: Dawn-Sealed Identity Depletion.** Each identity must publish a unique daily nonce derived from a fresh random seed at dawn, and the ledger records every seed ever used. A new identity costs one CPU-day of sequential work plus an irreversible lottery ticket whose loss probability compounds with each clone. Attackers pay linear compute per identity while honest agents amortize one seed across all actions; a nebula of clones therefore burns resources faster than it earns. Honest agents keep one lotus: a single seed reused across all their actions, making honesty strictly cheaper than cloning.
